titulo: Present tense in -are, negation and questions: Negation and frequency

aula.titulo: Present tense in -are, negation and questions
aula.objetivo: Conjugate regular -are verbs in the present tense, spell verbs like «mangiare» and «cercare», make negative sentences with «non» (including the double negative «non… mai»), and ask questions without the English helper «do».

blocos.titulo: Parliamo piano / Let us speak slowly
blocos.contexto: Ana and a classmate try out their Italian. Listen for where the little word «non» sits, and for how «sempre» is placed.

linhas.pt: — Hi, Ana! Do you speak Italian?

linhas.ru: — Sì, ma parlo solo un po'. E tu parli portoghese?
linhas.pt: — Yes, but I only speak a little. And do you speak Portuguese?
linhas.audio: Sì, ma parlo solo un po'. E tu parli portoghese?

linhas.ru: — No, non parlo portoghese, ma studio spagnolo.
linhas.pt: — No, I don't speak Portuguese, but I study Spanish.
linhas.audio: No, non parlo portoghese, ma studio spagnolo.

linhas.pt: — Then let's speak Italian, but slowly!

linhas.ru: — Perfetto! Io parlo sempre piano con gli amici.
linhas.pt: — Perfect! I always speak slowly with my friends.
linhas.audio: Perfetto! Io parlo sempre piano con gli amici.

blocos.titulo: Negation with «non» and the double negative
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: to make a sentence negative, put «non» directly before the verb: «Parlo tedesco» becomes «Non parlo tedesco». STEP 2: English needs the helper «do» («I do not speak»). Italian has no helper: just «non» + verb. STEP 3: the order is never «verb + not»: «Parlo non tedesco» is wrong. STEP 4: Italian requires a double negative. When a negative word like «mai» (never) comes after the verb, «non» must still stand before the verb: «Non mangio mai la pasta», literally «I do not eat never pasta». STEP 5: the same pattern works with «niente» (nothing) and «nessuno» (nobody): «Non mangio niente», «Non parlo con nessuno». STEP 6: if the negative word comes before the verb, «non» is dropped: «Nessuno parla tedesco» (nobody speaks German). With «mai» in first position («Mai mangio la pasta») it is possible but emphatic; in everyday speech, use «Non mangio mai la pasta». STEP 7: «No» answers the question and «non» negates the verb, so a full negative answer uses both: «No, non parlo tedesco».
blocos.comparacao: Standard English avoids double negatives: «I never eat pasta», not «I don't never eat pasta». Italian does the opposite: the second negative word needs the first one. Think of it as a frame: «non» + verb + negative word. This is not an error and does not turn the sentence positive, as it would in English.

erros.motivo: «Non» goes before the verb, never after it.
After the verb, «mai» needs «non» before the verb.
«No» is the answer; «non» is the negation inside the sentence.

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: the adverbs of frequency are «sempre» (always), «spesso» (often), «mai» (never) and the phrase «ogni giorno» (every day). STEP 2: unlike English, which puts the adverb before the main verb («I always speak»), Italian usually puts it after the verb: «Parlo sempre piano». STEP 3: «ogni giorno» goes at the end or the beginning: «Studio ogni giorno» or «Ogni giorno studio». STEP 4: «un po'» means «a little» and has an apostrophe because it is short for «un poco»: «Parlo un po'». STEP 5: «mai» in a question means «ever»: «Mangi mai la pasta?» is «Do you ever eat pasta?».
blocos.comparacao: English adverbs of frequency come before the verb («I always speak», «we often study»). Italian usually puts them after it. That is a small shift, and the easy way to remember it is to say the Italian sentence in this order: subject (hidden), verb, adverb.

exemplos.ru: Perfetto! Io parlo sempre piano con gli amici.
exemplos.pt: Perfect! I always speak slowly with my friends.

erros.motivo: «Ogni» always takes a singular noun, as English «every» does: «ogni giorno», never «ogni giorni».

itens.explicacao: Listen for the small word «non» at the start.
«Non… mai» is the double negative: both words are needed.

itens.enunciado: Which sentence means «I never eat pasta»?
itens.explicacao: After the verb, «mai» needs «non» in front of the verb.
«Non» is the negation inside a sentence.

blocos.enunciado: Say aloud three things you do not do, with «non», and one thing you never do with «non… mai».
Explain aloud, in English, why «Non mangio mai» is not a mistake. Where does the English «do» go in Italian?
